records.supported_name_scope: The complete generalized single source polygon is associated with Dore Lake: a broad northern basin and multiple southern lobes shown as one named lake on the WSA map. This is a generalized lake identity, not a surveyed shoreline or scalar-name approval.
correspondence_observations: The WSA map places Dore Lake south of Lac La Plonge, west of Smoothstone Lake and north of Sled/Beaupre lakes; the candidate is the broad lake in that arrangement.

The source polygon preserves the same broad northern body, western indentation, southwestern extensions, long south-central inlet and eastward/southeastern lobe visible on the map. The match uses the whole outline, not merely label location or a centroid.
The WSA map depicts islands and finer shoreline structure that the one-ring generalized source polygon omits. Adjacent separately mapped waterbodies are not treated as parts of Dore Lake.
name_scope_limits: The acquired official map and hydrometric index support the unaccented form Dore; the accented spelling supplied as a lead is not independently established by these sources.
The 2014 WSA map has an accuracy/currency disclaimer; its 2025 URL folder does not update the mapped content.
No formal naming record, effective naming date, present registry status, datum-transformed overlay or exact shoreline fit was established.

records.supported_name_scope: The complete generalized source polygon is associated with the single mapped Ennadai Lake across adjoining 65C and 65F sheets. The southwestern body and both main northern arms have continuous geographic/cartographic support. This is a generalized lake identity, not a surveyed shoreline or scalar-name approval.
correspondence_observations: Sheet 65C shows the elongated southwest-to-northeast main body labeled ENNADAI LAKE, including its southwest termination near Birch Bay, Caribou Point and eastern body near Halfway Bluff.

At the shared 61°N sheet boundary, sheet 65F continues the western and eastern northern arms; both are labeled ENNADAI LAKE. Their arrangement matches the two northern protrusions and intervening land indentation in the complete source polygon.

North End Lake is separately drawn and labeled east of the northeastern Ennadai arm. Its label is not evidence that the Ennadai candidate is a compound of two named lakes. No exact boundary-fit claim is made.

The generalized source polygon omits mapped islands and many fine shoreline inlets. The historic maps are in NAD27, while the source geographic coordinates have not been datum-transformed or surveyed against them.
name_scope_limits: 65C and 65F are complementary sheets of one 1979 thematic series using a base map with information current as of 1963; they are not independent current registry sources.
The 2019 CIRNAC narrative independently confirms government usage of Ennadai Lake but does not establish formal naming status or geographic extent.
No formal naming decision, current registry status, indigenous-language form, Korean form, quantitative georeferenced overlap or exact shoreline fit was verified.

publication_scope: Own factual observations, short labels, original URLs, exact response-body hashes and reproducible locators only; no official publication bodies, complete extracted texts, map images, crops or overlays.
